raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Supersedes #36173 and addresses its final review findings.

## Motivation

SGLang normally computes the top-p cutoff from the original probability distribution and intersects that support with top-k. Some sampling paths instead applied top-k, renormalized the remaining probabilities, and then applied top-p. That applies top-p to whatever probability mass happens to remain after top-k, making its effect unpredictable and inconsistent with other sampling paths using the same parameters.

The affected paths are the FlashInfer min-p path, the shared EAGLE-family/standalone/n-gram verifier, and the target-distribution builder shared by DFlash, DSpark, and UNO. UNO's separate compact top-k path also needed the same fix; its behavior could otherwise depend on other requests in the batch.

## Modifications

- Apply top-p before top-k in the FlashInfer min-p path.
- Apply the same ordering in the shared EAGLE-family, standalone, and n-gram verifier.
- Correct both the dense and sparse target distributions shared by DFlash, DSpark, and UNO.
- Preserve the sparse top-k path by translating the top-p cutoff into the renormalized top-k distribution using the top-k support's original probability mass.
- Apply the same correction to UNO's separate compact top-k path.
- Reject `min_p > 0` for built-in speculative decoding, where it is not currently applied.
- Add focused CUDA regression tests for each corrected implementation.

## Accuracy Tests

The regressions use probabilities `[0.35, 0.25, 0.20, 0.05, 0.03, ...]`, `top_k=4`, and `top_p=0.82`. The FlashInfer min-p case also uses `min_p=0.1`.

The original top-p nucleus includes token 3 because the probability mass before it is `0.80`. Applying and renormalizing top-k first changes that mass to `0.80 / 0.85`, causing token 3 to be incorrectly removed.

Validated rebased commit `50e6ca6b73cc49214b5e9e28068b187ac3d7de2f` on an NVIDIA H200 with Python 3.12.3, CUDA 13.0, PyTorch 2.13.0, FlashInfer 0.6.18, and Triton 3.7.1.

The consolidated `TestSamplingMaskCapture` class and `test_speculative_sampling.py` reported **18 passed, 6 subtests passed**, with zero failures, errors, or skips.

Each regression passed with the fix and failed its support/probability assertion with the pre-fix filtering:

| Path | With fix | Before fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| FlashInfer min-p | Pass | Support length 3 instead of 4 |
| EAGLE, using the production FlashInfer kernels | Pass | Token-3 probability mismatch |
| Shared target builder, dense | Pass | Token-3 probability mismatch |
| Shared target builder, sparse | Pass | Token-3 probability mismatch |
| UNO compact | Pass | Compact support probability mismatch |

The comparison used pre-fix filtering from public rebase base `d2a436446cca3d955358e7b4a5bf6881ea8591cd` with the same consolidated tests. For EAGLE, the pre-fix inline filtering was placed behind the extracted helper signature so the regression could exercise it.

Ruff 0.15.1, isort 7.0.0, Python syntax, Git whitespace checks, and registered-test checks pass. These CUDA results come from a separate GPU job. Upstream lint, title, and rebase checks pass; upstream GPU CI is waiting for the maintainer's `run-ci` label.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No end-to-end benchmark has been run.

The FlashInfer and EAGLE changes reorder existing filtering operations. The corrected sparse DFlash/DSpark/UNO path adds a full-vocabulary `logsumexp` reduction to recover the original probability mass represented by its top-k support. The UNO compact correction also adds the full-vocabulary `logsumexp` when top-p filtering is needed.

## Checklist

- [x] Format the code with Ruff.
- [x] Add unit tests.
- [x] No documentation change is required.
- [ ] Run upstream CI.
- [ ] Provide speed benchmark results.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

```

cd test/ && python3 registered/kernels/ops/speculative/test_dflash_sampling_filters.py
cd test/ && python3 registered/kernels/ops/speculative/test_eagle_sampling_filters.py
```

cc cmt

Thanks for the fix. The regression coverage itself is worth keeping: each case guards a different implementation (FlashInfer min-p branch, EAGLE verifier, DFlash dense/sparse, UNO compact), and the existing min-p capture test runs with `top_p=1.0`, so it never exercised this ordering. A few requests on how the tests are added, per `.claude/rules/unit-test-admission.md` and the `write-sglang-test` skill:

- [P3] Three new test files where existing files already fit. The rule says "New cases join an existing file in the same subsystem by default. Create a new file only when it needs a different fixture, dependency, owner, or CI contract", and none of those applies here. Impact: three more files and `est_time` registrations in `base-b-kernel-unit`, with the joint-filter coverage split across three places. Suggested placement:
  - `test_flashinfer_min_p.py` -> one more case in `test/registered/sampling/test_sampling_mask.py`. Its `_sample(probs, backend, top_k=..., top_p=..., min_p=...)` helper already drives `Sampler._sample_from_probs` for both `pytorch` and `flashinfer`, so no `get_exec` / `min_p_sampling_from_probs` patching is needed: run your distribution with `top_k=4, top_p=0.82, min_p=0.1` and assert the captured support is `{0, 1, 2, 3}`. This also moves a sampler test out of `kernels/ops/`, which is meant for kernel tests.
  - `test_eagle_sampling_filters.py` and `test_dflash_sampling_filters.py` -> `test/registered/kernels/ops/speculative/test_speculative_sampling.py`, which has the identical registration (`base-b-kernel-unit`, `1-gpu-large`) and already covers verifier target probabilities.
- [P3] The EAGLE case does not exercise the kernels the verifier uses. It injects `sgl_kernel.top_k_renorm_prob` / `top_p_renorm_prob`, while `eagle_sample` binds `flashinfer.sampling.top_k_renorm_probs` / `top_p_renorm_probs` on CUDA (and the Triton renorm on HIP). Impact: a FlashInfer-specific cutoff difference in the EAGLE path would still pass, so the case only pins the call order inside `_apply_joint_top_k_top_p`. Please inject the same functions the verifier imports.
- Evidence gap (not a bug): the PR body shows the FlashInfer case failing on the pre-fix code, but not the EAGLE, DFlash dense/sparse, or UNO compact cases. The admission rule asks that each regression case be verified to fail before the fix and pass after; could you add that result once the cases are consolidated?

cc cmt

- [P2] `lint` still fails on the rebased head (`f8f9151`) because of the isort hook, which blocks merge. The repo's `.isort.cfg` sets `known_first_party=sglang`, so third-party imports (`torch`, `flashinfer`, `sgl_kernel`) and `sglang.*` imports must be separated by a blank line. This PR drops that blank line in `python/sglang/srt/speculative/uno_utils.py`, and the two new files `test/registered/kernels/ops/speculative/test_dflash_sampling_filters.py` and `test_eagle_sampling_filters.py` are missing it too; the hook reports `Fixing ...` for exactly these three files. Running this from the repo root should fix it:

  ```bash
  pre-commit run isort --files python/sglang/srt/speculative/uno_utils.py test/registered/kernels/ops/speculative/test_dflash_sampling_filters.py test/registered/kernels/ops/speculative/test_eagle_sampling_filters.py
  ```

CUDA before-and-after validation is still pending. I’ll follow up with results for all five paths once the ML job completes.

Thanks for the fix. The regression coverage itself is worth keeping: each case guards a different implementation (FlashInfer min-p branch, EAGLE verifier, DFlash dense/sparse, UNO compact), and the existing min-p capture test runs with `top_p=1.0`, so it never exercised this ordering. A few requests on how the tests are added, per `.claude/rules/unit-test-admission.md` and the `write-sglang-test` skill:

- [P3] Three new test files where existing files already fit. The rule says "New cases join an existing file in the same subsystem by default. Create a new file only when it needs a different fixture, dependency, owner, or CI contract", and none of those applies here. Impact: three more files and `est_time` registrations in `base-b-kernel-unit`, with the joint-filter coverage split across three places. Suggested placement:
  - `test_flashinfer_min_p.py` -> one more case in `test/registered/sampling/test_sampling_mask.py`. Its `_sample(probs, backend, top_k=..., top_p=..., min_p=...)` helper already drives `Sampler._sample_from_probs` for both `pytorch` and `flashinfer`, so no `get_exec` / `min_p_sampling_from_probs` patching is needed: run your distribution with `top_k=4, top_p=0.82, min_p=0.1` and assert the captured support is `{0, 1, 2, 3}`. This also moves a sampler test out of `kernels/ops/`, which is meant for kernel tests.
  - `test_eagle_sampling_filters.py` and `test_dflash_sampling_filters.py` -> `test/registered/kernels/ops/speculative/test_speculative_sampling.py`, which has the identical registration (`base-b-kernel-unit`, `1-gpu-large`) and already covers verifier target probabilities.
- [P3] The EAGLE case does not exercise the kernels the verifier uses. It injects `sgl_kernel.top_k_renorm_prob` / `top_p_renorm_prob`, while `eagle_sample` binds `flashinfer.sampling.top_k_renorm_probs` / `top_p_renorm_probs` on CUDA (and the Triton renorm on HIP). Impact: a FlashInfer-specific cutoff difference in the EAGLE path would still pass, so the case only pins the call order inside `_apply_joint_top_k_top_p`. Please inject the same functions the verifier imports.
- Evidence gap (not a bug): the PR body shows the FlashInfer case failing on the pre-fix code, but not the EAGLE, DFlash dense/sparse, or UNO compact cases. The admission rule asks that each regression case be verified to fail before the fix and pass after; could you add that result once the cases are consolidated?

cc cmt

- [P2] `lint` still fails on the rebased head (`f8f9151`) because of the isort hook, which blocks merge. The repo's `.isort.cfg` sets `known_first_party=sglang`, so third-party imports (`torch`, `flashinfer`, `sgl_kernel`) and `sglang.*` imports must be separated by a blank line. This PR drops that blank line in `python/sglang/srt/speculative/uno_utils.py`, and the two new files `test/registered/kernels/ops/speculative/test_dflash_sampling_filters.py` and `test_eagle_sampling_filters.py` are missing it too; the hook reports `Fixing ...` for exactly these three files. Running this from the repo root should fix it:

